newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-O'MEARA WINS AT PEBBLE BEACH FOR RECORD FIFTH TIME.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-O'MEARA WINS AT PEBBLE BEACH FOR RECORD FIFTH TIME.

text.p: Mark O'Meara held off a charging Tiger Woods, his neighbour and "little friend," to win the Pebble Beach National Pro-Am for a record fifth time on Sunday.
O'Meara shot his fourth straight round of 67 to finish at 20 under par, a tournament scoring record by three strokes.
Woods and overnight leader David Duval were tied for second at 19 under par. Woods had weekend rounds at Pebble of 63-64, while Duval birdied the last two holes to shoot a one-under round of 71.

"All I can say is that it is a tremendous thrill to win this championship again for the fifth time," said O'Meara. "I don't think I played at my best. I wasn't knocking flags down like I saw my little friend Tiger doing in front of me, but I stayed patient and did what I had to do."
Woods, who started the round seven strokes behind, picked up five birdies in the first eight holes, and after birdieing the 12th was just a stroke off of O'Meara's lead.

With three holes to play Woods was two strokes behind, but put pressure on O'Meara by hitting a wedge to four feet on the 16th and a seven-iron to four feet at the 17th, and then sinking both birdie putts.
O'Meara responded by chipping in for birdie from 15 feet on number 16, then sinking a 12-foot putt for birdie on the 17th.
After hearing the roars for the birdie which brought O'Meara's lead back to two strokes, Woods decided to go for the green on the par-five 18th.
He hit a three-wood from the edge of the right rough onto the putting surface -- the first to reach that green in two all week -- some 40 feet from the cup.

Woods couldn't sink the eagle putt to force the playoff. "I feel both disappointment and excitement. I would have been in a playoff if I hadn't made the one bogey on number 13. I made a good run for it, but it was too little, too late."
Woods and O'Meara are neighbours in Florida, and see one another every day when they are home.
"We've talked about it at home, wouldn't it be great if we could duel it out head to head," said Woods. "I love Mark to death, I think it's great that he won."

With his fifth pro win at Pebble Beach -- and he also won the Cal State Amateur here -- O'Meara joined an elite group of golfers with five or more victories in a single event: Walter Hagen, Ben Hogan, Sam Snead, Arnold Palmer and Jack Nicklaus.
"I wish I could figure out why I do so well here," said O'Meara. "I guess there's someone up there, up above the Monterey Peninsula, who is a huge Mark O'Meara fan."
Five of his 13 career victories have come at Pebble Beach. His 72-hole total of 20-under 268 broke the tournament record of 271, set by Peter Jacobsen in 1995.
For O'Meara, 40, facing down the 21-year-old Woods made this win special.

"I think there was an advantage for me, not playing with him and seeing him blow it by me 50 yards. He was applying the pressure, and applying the pressure, but I knew what I had to do to hold him off. I feel like it's, like, 'all right for the 40-year-olds.'"

The win was the 13th of O'Meara's 17 year PGA Tour career. The $342,000 first prize, O'Meara's biggest payday, put him on top of the 1997 money list with $440,460. In second place is Woods, whose $167,200 earnings this week gave him a $403,450 total for his three starts this year.
Duval brought a three-stroke lead into the final round, but had his second straight second-place finish in the event. He is winless with six second-place finishes in two-plus years on the PGA Tour.
